neighbours.label: the determiner after a preposition in a phrase that says in what respect or how far a judgement holds: 'by any means', 'for that matter', 'remarkable in its/their <quality>' (the + pole is 'as far as'); the same determiners as plain possessives or objects stay quiet
fire: The exam was not difficult by any means, yet half the class failed.
She has never visited Spain, or for that matter anywhere in Europe.
The cathedral is breathtaking in its scale and detail.
The two proposals are nearly identical in their wording.
It is not a perfect film by any means, though the acting is superb.
The essay is remarkable in its honesty about failure.
Nobody in the office, or for that matter in the whole building, had a key.
The reforms were modest in their aims but lasting in effect.
quiet: The exam was not difficult for most students, yet half the class failed.
She has never visited Spain, though her sister lives in Europe.
The cathedral lost its spire in the storm of 1890.
The two authors revised their wording after the review.
It is not a perfect film, and any critic will tell you so.
The essay made that point about failure quite well.
Nobody in the office had any key to that building.
The reforms achieved their aims within a decade.

notes: Probing: 'by any means' 0.56, 'for that matter' 0.67, 'ambitious in its scope' 0.44, 'staggering in its breadth' 0.49, 'differ in their approach' 0.22, 'by definition' 0.17; 'sold its headquarters' 0.02, 'did not have any money' 0.03.
